the canonical view for an object is determined by the following factors in order of decreasing importance: (i) the shape of the object, (ii) the function of the object, and (iii) the way the object is used.

the preferred or canonical view of a 3D object is determined by its geometrical, functional, and experiential attributes, but the relative importance of these attributes depends on the context in which the object is viewed.
the canonical views for familiar objects are determined by a combination of the geometrical attributes of an object and the experiential and functional attributes of an object.
